newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Postal Service said vulnerable to competition.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Postal Service said vulnerable to competition.

text.p: The U.S. Postal Service is highly vulnerable to increased competition from private delivery firms, according to a new General Accounting Office report to be released Monday, The Washington Post reported.
The report questions whether the federal agency can continue to justify the economic grounds for its letter monopoly, the paper said.

The study by the investigative arm of Congress warns of profound consequences of relaxing the 200-year old laws that give the Postal Service a monopoly on the delivery of letters. It suggests that allowing private firms to deliver mail could seriously jeopardize the government agency unless it lowers its prices and improves the quality of its services.
The report noted that private delivery firms now control 85 percent of the market for overnight deliveries, which Congress opened to competition in 1979.
It said it was not clear wehter the underlying economic basis for keeping the letter monopoly remained valid.
